UnitStatement: Model fallback chain: opts.model -> CHIRALITY_GLOBAL_MODEL or instruction-root frontmatter -> runtime default.

Tools fallback chain: opts.tools -> persona frontmatter/defaults -> runtime default; max turns: opts.maxTurns -> persona frontmatter/defaults -> runtime default; mode and persona use request/session values before runtime defaults.

Settings posture: shipped SDK options use settingSources: []; development-only project settings may use ['project'] only behind explicit environment configuration; user and local setting sources are not permitted in shipped builds.
Tool mapping posture: opts.tools maps only to registered SDK built-ins or Chirality MCP tools, and unknown names produce structured validation errors.
Permission boundary posture: allowedTools is not a restriction boundary by itself; restrictions depend on deny rules, mode policy, hooks, canUseTool, and/or dontAsk posture.
Max-turn guard: resolved maxTurns is passed into SDK options so runaway loops stop and terminal max-turn errors can be persisted; exact error mapping is owned by adjacent runtime/event deliverables.

SdkOptionsBuilder exists to keep SDK request construction deterministic, explicit, and governed while Chirality adopts the Claude Agent SDK as a replaceable implementation substrate.

The builder should translate Chirality-owned session state, resolved runtime options, prompt/tool policy, settings posture, and resume metadata into SDK-facing options without allowing SDK defaults or ambient settings to redefine product behavior.

Principle: determinism before convenience; for the same session, persona, mode, option set, SDK version, MCP server set, and policy input, the builder should produce stable option values, stable tool ordering, and stable visible metadata.

Principle: settings isolation is a release boundary; shipped builds use settingSources: [], and development-only project settings require explicit environment enablement and must not include user or local sources.
Principle: policy adequacy is checked before option construction; the builder should not normalize missing governed policy into permissive SDK defaults.

If required settings, tool, permission, hook, MCP, or subagent policy inputs are absent, explicitly unresolved, or contradictory, the builder should fail closed or return a structured integration error before constructing SDK options.

Principle: allowedTools is not a safety boundary; treat it as SDK auto-approval posture, with restricted modes requiring deny rules, disallowed tools, hooks, canUseTool, dontAsk, or the PKG-06 overlay as applicable.

Principle: adapter metadata is allowed but public semantic leakage is not; SDK-specific names and SDK package version may appear in adapter-local and safe runtime metadata as runtime-adapter evidence, while public Chirality APIs, canonical events, and governance records remain Chirality-owned.

Principle: prefer explicit unknowns over plausible SDK detail; exact SDK TypeScript option fields not confirmed by local accepted source or the first-adapter probe should remain TBD to avoid making an unverified SDK version look authoritative.
Consideration on fallback implementation: keep fallback resolution pure and testable, emit warnings for unknown option keys, and do not let unknown fields affect behavior.

Consideration on settings posture: make shipped/development posture an explicit input or environment-derived policy and record the selected posture in safe metadata; shipped option construction omits ambient settings via settingSources: [], and development project settings are admitted only by the explicit development policy path.
Consideration on tool registry: resolve requested tool names against a deterministic registry of SDK built-ins and Chirality MCP tools, with unknown names failing before SDK request construction.
Consideration on hooks and permissions: accept hook/callback/deny policy inputs but do not overclaim that this slice fully implements PKG-06 permission semantics.

Consideration on resume and session linkage: include resume/session fields only through the engine/session contract and safe adapter metadata, with SDK transcripts remaining secondary to Chirality events.
Consideration on subagents: treat subagent option construction as policy-gated and fail-closed until the governance bridge supplies restricted child definitions.
Trade-off SDK defaults vs explicit options: prefer explicit Chirality options and recorded posture to prevent ambient settings and SDK defaults from becoming product semantics.

Trade-off early tool exposure vs controlled sequence: prefer read-only and registered tools first, deferring write/bash/subagent execution until overlays and hooks are active, matching roadmap sequence and avoiding permission boundary overclaiming.

Trade-off rich SDK metadata vs provider-neutral core: keep SDK metadata local to adapter/runtime metadata with public APIs and canonical events in Chirality terms to preserve engine replaceability and conformance testing.

Trade-off immediate exact SDK field design vs probe-backed API: use TBD for exact fields until SDK version/probe confirms current TypeScript APIs, avoiding encoding stale or guessed upstream SDK behavior.

Example fallback trace: when opts.model is TBD, CHIRALITY_GLOBAL_MODEL is set, and instruction-root and runtime defaults are available, the resolved model is CHIRALITY_GLOBAL_MODEL with no warnings unless unknown option keys are present.
Example settings posture for a shipped build: settingSources = [] and visible metadata includes settings-source posture 'shipped-empty'.
Example settings posture for development-only explicit project settings: settingSources = ['project'], visible metadata posture 'development-project', and user/local setting sources remain forbidden.

Example tool resolution: Read maps to a registered SDK built-in if available, mcp__chirality__status_read maps to a registered Chirality MCP tool, and unknown_tool returns a structured validation error before SDK request construction.
